Dana — thanks for the context. Quick note from our side: our CFO has a board prep travel week from Aug 26–29, and several execs are on the same itinerary, which means demos with the full decision team will be hard to get on those dates. Given OrchidTech's procurement lead availability and the upcoming budget lock, I recommend two options:

1) Short live 30–45m exec-facing demo this week (no deep Q&A) and circulate a full recorded walkthrough + MMP so your team can review while procurement returns.
2) Pause scheduled live sessions until after your budget close (target week of Sep 7) and plan a launch-ready pilot conversation once PO timing is clearer.

If you want us to prioritize an exec slot this week I can try to free a 30-minute window (no deep tech deep-dive). Otherwise I'm inclined to align post-budget so we avoid repeated rebooking.

I can share a mutual action plan and SOW draft to align expectations — Marissa, could you prepare the MAP and tentative SOW and tag the calendar with both options? Ben — FYI in case we want to offer a one-off credit if they need to push pilot start because of PO timing.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Looping back with a pragmatic approach from Sales Ops: we've seen Orchid-like procurement timelines slip ~7–12 business days around quarter close. Proposal:

- Offer the recorded technical walkthrough + a 30-min executive highlight session (non-technical) this week — helps keep momentum with execs.
- Send a concise mutual-action-plan (attached) that maps dates to deliverables and PO owner. If PO ETA slips beyond Sep 3, propose we hold the pilot kickoff until Sep 7-10.
- As a courtesy for the inconvenience, authorize a $5k pilot credit contingent on PO receipt within 30 days of kickoff.

Attached: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (editable) and a clean SOW stub (SOW-draft-v2.pdf). Marissa, can you put tentative calendar blocks for: Aug 26 (30m exec highlight) and Sep 8 (90m technical kickoff)?

Thanks — Ben

Appreciate the pilot credit offer — that will help clear the internal conversation.
